story: At 4:17 on a breezy Saturday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary welcomes Rosa into his kitchen, where the cornbread is heading into the oven and his golf cart waits in the driveway with its lights and speakers still pending Architectural Review. Rosa, hopeful, asks him to join her welcome dinner Friday night with Donna and Hal, promising him a chance to talk about parade lights. Across town at the Rec Center, the determined Donna studies the ladder standings to plan which rivals she and Gary must beat first, while Hal, dutifully counting pink flamingos on Magnolia Loop, notes which ones the hedge hides from view.
events: Donna (ladder standings board): Study the ladder standings to see who Gary and I need to beat first
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count only the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest

gary.thought_process: Rosa just walked in and I've got the cornbread batter going for her dinner. I'm stubborn about the cart, but I filed the Architectural Review request and the lights and speakers can't go on until it's approved, so I shouldn't pretend otherwise. Best thing to do is greet her warmly, tell her the cornbread's underway, and ask if she wants a look at the cart. That keeps me useful and chatty, which is what I like.

parameters.content: Rosa! Come on in, the cornbread batter's mixed and the oven's heating up. Want to see the cart while it bakes? Lights and speakers are still waiting on Architectural Review, but she's looking good.

donna.thought_process: I already reserved the Tuesday two-hour slot at the kiosk last tick, so that task is done. Nobody is around to talk to, and I'm at the Rec Center with the ladder standings board right here. Checking where we sit gives me something concrete to work with for recruiting Gary. After that I should head home to get ready for Rosa's Friday supper plans and my deviled eggs.

parameters.content: Study the ladder standings to see who Gary and I need to beat first

hal.thought_process: I'm alone on Magnolia Loop. Rosa says Donna's extras are behind the hedge, and my reflections say I'd rather keep the peace and my Friday dinner than play referee. Still, the law is the law: only flamingos visible from the street count under L-02. The flock object is right here, so I can verify by the book, count what's actually visible from the street, and note whether the hedge screens the rest. That keeps me fair, which is what I want Donna to trust me about.

parameters.content: Count only the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest

rosa.thought_process: I just walked into Gary's house and he's the only one here. I want all three neighbors at my table Friday, and Gary is the one I haven't pinned down yet. Hal is already helping him with the Architectural Review form, so that's in motion. I shouldn't repeat old lines, so I'll greet him warmly and give him a concrete invitation to the welcome dinner, and ask him to bring his appetite and maybe a cart-lighting story.

parameters.content: Gary, good, I caught you home. I'm hosting a welcome dinner Friday night and I want you at my table with Donna and Hal. Can I count on you? I'll even let you talk about the parade lights.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
